nodes.label: HCT Color Space
nodes.rationale: HCT was chosen because it enables flexible, predictable color manipulation while providing perceptually meaningful dimensions (hue, chroma, tone). Traditional spaces like RGB do not adequately capture relationships between colors, whereas HCT supports both accessibility (via tone-based contrast) and expressive design.

nodes.label: DynamicScheme (Concept)
nodes.rationale: DynamicScheme abstracts exact color values from app developers, who only choose color roles. This separation allows the system to swap underlying tonal palette values without breaking UI structure.

nodes.label: Fidelity Tone Adjustment
nodes.rationale: Colors in certain hue/tone combinations cannot reach target chroma because HCT gamut is not uniform. Fidelity adjustment corrects these 'impossible' colors by adjusting tone to match source or reach target chroma.

nodes.label: HCT Color Space (Technical)
nodes.rationale: HCT combines CAM16-JCH hue/chroma with L* (CIELAB) tone. This hybrid was chosen so tone is perceptually uniform (enabling reliable contrast calculation) while hue and chroma follow a color appearance model that accounts for viewing conditions.

nodes.label: Contrast Ratio
nodes.rationale: Contrast ratio is defined using the Y component of CIEXYZ (not hue or chroma) because Y directly captures luminance/brightness as perceived by the human visual system, making it the most reliable single-axis measure for legibility.

nodes.label: QuantizerCelebi
nodes.rationale: Celebi quantizer is recommended because it combines Wu (fast initial clustering) with WSMeans (quality refinement), balancing speed and color fidelity for theme extraction from images.

nodes.label: ViewingConditions (Swift)
nodes.rationale: ViewingConditions caches intermediate CAM16 conversion values that only depend on the environment (not the color), providing speed-up while enabling color relativity as described by Josef Albers.
